events.title: Fundamentals of Tai Chi at SCCC
events.description:
Located: Sebastopol Community Cultural Center

Tai Chi is a popular exercise that utilizes slow and sequential body patterns combined with relaxing breathing exercises. While it is a great fitness regimen for all ages, it can be especially helpful for seniors by reducing the risk of dementia, depression, and seniors falling down. Other possible benefits including increasing bone density, immune system enhancement, and balance improvement. This class is very popular and for Members only. Due to the growing popularity of senior center classes and as part of our commitment to providing a consistent and seamless experience for all participants, we can no longer accommodate waitlists for classes. This means that all participants must sign up for classes in advance to secure a spot.

events.title: Harmonic Method for Wellbeing
events.address: Sebastopol Area Senior Center, 167 N High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472, USA
events.description:
Join us as we create a space of connection through toning and rhythm. By vocalizing together—first in unison and then in harmony—we will foster a sense of individual awareness within a supportive, safe group environment. As the session progresses, we will co-create intricate melodic and rhythmic patterns, drawing inspiration from Circle Singing.
Human connection is essential to our well-being. But how can we enhance our ability to give and receive meaningful interactions? Despite our philosophical, social, or personal differences, we all share the experience of being vibrational beings immersed in fields of sound. Our voice is the most intimate, authentic expression of who we are—a window into our emotional and physical health.
In this playful, exploratory session, we will:
Tune into our inner world through silence and listening,
Explore the connection between breath and voice,
Discover vocal resonance, placement, and projection,
Experience the vibrational power of overtones,
Harmonize with others by blending tones and intervals,
Reflect on what harmony feels like and how it can deepen our access to intuition.
After our exploration, we will come together in joyful co-creation with our voices. This group is led by the wonderful Jim Paschal. Learn more about Jim's "Harmonic Method for Well-Being" on his website: Harmonic Method for Well-Being.
Register online at sebastopolseniorcenter.org using your membership key tag code.  OR CALL 707-829-2440

Most people will bring their own projects, but we always have hooks, needles, and yarn and sometimes we will offer a project with instructions that people may choose to make. Let us know what you would like to learn this year. We now have a working sewing machine for people to use. For beginners, I will bring is some fabric to make pillowcases. If you have a project that you would like to work on, bring in your fabric and thread and you can use the machine.

We share ideas, skills, and encouragement with each other.
This summer we will be adding, weaving, and decorative mending to our regular projects of knitting and crocheting.
Children can come if they are accompanied one to one with an adult.

events.description:
As we age we lose friends. Some die, some move away, some just... are gone. This is a group for older guys to make friends with other older guys. What do we usually talk about with other guys: sports, politics, the weather? Not in this group. In this group we talk about what's important to us, things like what's going on with our families, what we're glad we did in the past and what we wish we'd done. We talk about what makes us human, and in doing so we discover the many ways we're alike and the ways we're different. In the process we make friends, good friends, friends that we're pleased to have in our lives.

events.title: Garden Volunteer Day
events.description:
Join us for Volunteer Day in the garden! 

Walk-ins are always welcome – just show up! AND we kindly encourage you to RSVP by clicking the button below (for groups of 6 or more reach out to oaec@oaec.org to schedule so that we can best accommodate your group). Garden volunteers must be 16 years old to participate. 

We serve a homemade garden-based vegetarian lunch for those who come to volunteer for at least 3 hours. We will take a break at 12:30 to eat. Come for part or all of the day – we are happy to have your helping hands for as long as you can participate.

What to bring: In addition to a water bottle, we suggest bringing everything you’ll need to be comfortable outside in all weather – rain gear, an extra layer, hat, sunscreen, sturdy shoes, etc. Bring your own work gloves, if you have them. 

Please park in the upper lot near the nursery. Read our Contact & Directions page for more arrival information.

PLEASE CHECK THE RSVP FORM FOR HOLIDAYS AND OTHER CLOSURES

events.title: The Native Story of Sonoma County
events.venue: Sonoma County Library: Roseland Regional Library
events.address: 470 Sebastopol Rd., Santa Rosa, CA, 95407, US
events.org: Sonoma County Library: Roseland Regional Library
events.sourceLabel: Sonoma County Library: Roseland Regional Library calendar
events.description:
Professor Paul Steward presents a lecture and discussion of Native American history from ancient times to contemporary, with a focus on Sonoma County peoples' perspective.

---------------------------------------------------------------

Paul Steward is an accomplished educator, professional musician, and enrolled tribal member of the Elem Indian Colony of Pomo Indians. Serving as a Lecturer in Native American and American Indian Studies at San Francisco State University and Sonoma State University since 2016, he specializes in California Indian history, culture, and tribal relations. Parallel to his academic career, Steward is a celebrated singer, songwriter, and guitarist with over 20 years of professional experience. By uniquely blending traditional Pomo rhythms, language, and instruments with modern blues and soul, his work creates a vital cultural bridge that has earned him prestigious accolades, including the Native American Music Awards and recognition as a Yerba Buena Center for the Arts honoree.

events.title: Day Trip- Western Railway Museum
events.description:
A Living History Experience

Step back in time as you explore the museum’s fascinating exhibits and ride into history aboard vintage electric trains!
The museum showcases historic electric interurban trains, vintage streetcars, and the largest collection of Sacramento Northern Railway equipment in existence. All trains, streetcars, and trolleys are historic.
Enjoy a 50-minute round-trip train excursion through the scenic Delta, offering plenty of time to soak in the nostalgia and beautiful views.
Following the train ride, enjoy a docent-led museum tour and learn more about the history behind these remarkable pieces of transportation.
Afterward, lunch is on your own in downtown Suisun on the waterfront. Explore the quaint town, choose from one of the many local restaurants, or bring your own lunch and enjoy it in the waterfront park.

Meet at Sebastopol Mt. Olive Church
Bus Departs 8:15AM | Return: 5:00PM
Lunch is not included.

events.title: Bennett Friedman Jazz Quartet
events.description: The concert will feature guitarist Randy Vincent, bassist Robb Fisher, drummer Kendrick Freeman, and saxophonist Bennett Friedman.Randy Vincent has been teaching jazz guitar at Sonoma State University since 1981. He has performed with Bobby Hutcherson, Joe Henderson, and Dizzy Gillespie. Vincent has authored six jazz guitar books, published by Sher Music Co. Bassist Robb Fisher toured and recorded with the legendary Cal Tjader for more than six years, anchoring Tjader's Grammy Award-winning album, "La Onda Va Bien," and Grammy-nominated album, "Gozame Pero Ya." He has also worked extensively with and recorded for jazz and Latin artists, including Chet Baker, Art Pepper, Carmen McRae, Tania Mar��a, Clare Fischer, Rob Schneiderman, Eddie Marshall, Dick Whittington, and Anita O'Day.Kendrick Freeman has a background in both drum set and hand drums, having studied with American artists and musicians from Ghana, Congo, and the Caribbean, with an emphasis on Haitian music. Freeman leads a jazz ensemble at Sonoma State University. Saxophonist Bennett Friedman has performed at the Monterey Jazz Festival, the Stanford Jazz Workshop, the San Jose Jazz Festival, the Healdsburg Jazz Festival, the Monterey Bay Blues Festival, and the Russian River Jazz Festival. He has been featured as a soloist with Frank Sinatra, Rosemary Clooney, Natalie Cole, and Marvin Gaye. Friedman has taught Jazz Studies at Santa Rosa Junior College since 1977. events.title: Harmonic Method for Wellbeing
events.address: Sebastopol Area Senior Center, 167 N High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472, USA
events.description:
Join us as we create a space of connection through toning and rhythm. By vocalizing together—first in unison and then in harmony—we will foster a sense of individual awareness within a supportive, safe group environment. As the session progresses, we will co-create intricate melodic and rhythmic patterns, drawing inspiration from Circle Singing.
Human connection is essential to our well-being. But how can we enhance our ability to give and receive meaningful interactions? Despite our philosophical, social, or personal differences, we all share the experience of being vibrational beings immersed in fields of sound. Our voice is the most intimate, authentic expression of who we are—a window into our emotional and physical health.
In this playful, exploratory session, we will:
Tune into our inner world through silence and listening,
Explore the connection between breath and voice,
Discover vocal resonance, placement, and projection,
Experience the vibrational power of overtones,
Harmonize with others by blending tones and intervals,
Reflect on what harmony feels like and how it can deepen our access to intuition.
After our exploration, we will come together in joyful co-creation with our voices. This group is led by the wonderful Jim Paschal. Learn more about Jim's "Harmonic Method for Well-Being" on his website: Harmonic Method for Well-Being.

events.title: Sourdough from Scratch with Monica Flaherty at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
events.address: Gold Ridge Organic Farm, 3387 Canfield Rd, Sebastopol, California, 95472
events.description:
Join us for a 3-hour hands-on sourdough making class at Gold Ridge Organic Farms, led by Monica Flaherty of the Sebastopol Sourdough Company. Spend three immersive hours in our charming Apple Cottage learning the art and science of sourdough bread making.
Monica will walk you through everything you need to know — how wild yeast and fermentation work, why sourdough differs from commercial yeast bread, and how to read your dough. You’ll also cover starter care and feeding, mixing and hydration ratios, shaping and scoring techniques, and the secrets to achieving that perfect crust and open crumb.
Every guest will leave with an active starter, a feeding schedule and care guide, a shaped dough in a banneton ready to bake at home, and their very own apron to take home as a keepsake. The experience also includes a ride across the farm on our beloved apple-themed trolley to the Apple Cottage.

events.sourceLabel: Sonoma County Library: Central Santa Rosa Library calendar
events.description:
Immerse yourself in North Indian Classical music featuring sitar and tabla.

---------------------------------------------------------------

Arjun K. Verma is an Indian-American sitarist and composer. Beginning with his father, Roop Verma, and continuing with the legendary Ali Akbar Khan and his son Alam Khan, Arjun’s meticulous training has imbued him with a rich musicality that encompasses both the profound majesty and the exhilaration of North Indian classical music.
Hailed by the New York Times as a “fine sitarist,” Arjun shares the jewels of his cultural heritage in a manner that is fresh, modern, and relevant, while maintaining a high standard of traditional integrity.

events.description:
As we age we lose friends. Some die, some move away, some just... are gone. This is a group for older guys to make friends with other older guys. What do we usually talk about with other guys: sports, politics, the weather? Not in this group. In this group we talk about what's important to us, things like what's going on with our families, what we're glad we did in the past and what we wish we'd done. We talk about what makes us human, and in doing so we discover the many ways we're alike and the ways we're different. In the process we make friends, good friends, friends that we're pleased to have in our lives.

events.description:
Join us for Volunteer Day in the garden! 

Walk-ins are always welcome – just show up! AND we kindly encourage you to RSVP by clicking the button below (for groups of 6 or more reach out to oaec@oaec.org to schedule so that we can best accommodate your group). Garden volunteers must be 16 years old to participate. 

We serve a homemade garden-based vegetarian lunch for those who come to volunteer for at least 3 hours. We will take a break at 12:30 to eat. Come for part or all of the day – we are happy to have your helping hands for as long as you can participate.

What to bring: In addition to a water bottle, we suggest bringing everything you’ll need to be comfortable outside in all weather – rain gear, an extra layer, hat, sunscreen, sturdy shoes, etc. Bring your own work gloves, if you have them. 

Please park in the upper lot near the nursery. Read our Contact & Directions page for more arrival information.

Tai Chi is a popular exercise that utilizes slow and sequential body patterns combined with relaxing breathing exercises. Title: Fall Risk Screening
Time: By Appointment Only; No walk-ins.
Facilitator: SASC Fall Prevention Team
Cost: Members $5  Non-members  $10

Pre-registration is required.

Determine if you are at risk for falling by completing a series of simple physical and cognitive tests designed to assess your balance, strength, and mobility.

Understanding your risk factors empowers you to take preventive steps through exercises, home safety modifications, and lifestyle changes.

Screening performed by a team of professionals including John Johnson. John is a retired physical therapist assistant and former FallProof! instructor. He was a volunteer "master trainer" for the Matter of Balance fall prevention program in Sonoma County, administered by the Adult & Aging Division of the County Human Services Department.  

Pre-registration is required.  Call us at (707) 829-2440 to schedule your screening.
Will take place OFFSITE at Wischemann Hall.

events.title: Olio Nuovo Harvest and Milling Experience at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
events.address: Gold Ridge Organic Farm, 3387 Canfield Rd, Sebastopol, California, 95472
events.description:
Join us for an unforgettable behind-the-scenes journey into the heart of our olive harvest season. This experience offers a rare opportunity to see how our award-winning olive oil is crafted, from the branches of our olive trees to the first drops of the season’s oil.
Your journey begins with a guided tour of our 88-acre organic farm. You’ll step into the orchards to watch our expert team harvest fresh olives straight from the trees at their peak of flavor.
Next, you’ll visit our state-of-the-art olive oil mill, where you’ll learn about the milling process and see the olives pressed into vibrant, fresh Olio Nuovo, the celebrated “new oil” prized by culinary enthusiasts for its brilliant green hue and robust, peppery finish.
The highlight comes right at the source: tasting fresh Olio Nuovo straight from the mill just moments after the olives are crushed.
Book now to secure your spot for this rare, behind-the-scenes look at our harvest traditions.
Important Notes:
*Please wear comfortable shoes suitable for walking on a working farm
*This outdoor experience may be canceled due to wet weather. Full refund available.

events.title: Harmonic Method for Wellbeing
events.address: Sebastopol Area Senior Center, 167 N High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472, USA
events.description:
Join us as we create a space of connection through toning and rhythm. By vocalizing together—first in unison and then in harmony—we will foster a sense of individual awareness within a supportive, safe group environment. As the session progresses, we will co-create intricate melodic and rhythmic patterns, drawing inspiration from Circle Singing.
Human connection is essential to our well-being. But how can we enhance our ability to give and receive meaningful interactions? Despite our philosophical, social, or personal differences, we all share the experience of being vibrational beings immersed in fields of sound. Our voice is the most intimate, authentic expression of who we are—a window into our emotional and physical health.
In this playful, exploratory session, we will:
Tune into our inner world through silence and listening,
Explore the connection between breath and voice,
Discover vocal resonance, placement, and projection,
Experience the vibrational power of overtones,
Harmonize with others by blending tones and intervals,
Reflect on what harmony feels like and how it can deepen our access to intuition.
After our exploration, we will come together in joyful co-creation with our voices. This group is led by the wonderful Jim Paschal. Learn more about Jim's "Harmonic Method for Well-Being" on his website: Harmonic Method for Well-Being.
Register online at sebastopolseniorcenter.org using your membership key tag code.  OR CALL 707-829-2440

Explore topics related to death, dying, grief, loss, caregiving, aging, and legacy in a welcoming community setting.
Rooted in the international Death Café model, offering open, agenda-free conversation and reflection.
Participate in guided discussions, reflective writing, and occasional readings or prompts.
Share experiences, ask questions, and connect with others in a respectful, supportive environment.

events.title: 19th Annual Doris Dickenson Young Writers Contest Awards Ceremony
events.org: Sonoma County Library: Guerneville Regional Library
events.sourceLabel: Sonoma County Library: Guerneville Regional Library calendar
events.description:
FORMATION:
The Young Writers Contest was established to celebrate young writers and artists and to honor Doris Dickenson, a longtime Guerneville resident. Doris devoted her life to teaching, raising her four children, and volunteering with community organizations. She was a member of the River Friends of the Library, the Russian River Senior Center, and the Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods. She also had a keen interest in genealogy and co-authored several biographies and DVDs about the Armstrong family with Carmen Finley.

PURPOSE:
To foster the next generation of thinkers and creators, our goal is to inspire youth to think critically and express their creativity by writing about relevant, timely topics.

ELIGIBILITY:
To enter the contest, students must be in grades 5-9 and live in Sonoma County. We strongly encourage all local students to enter.

DATES/TIMES:
Submission due date: Friday, October 16, 2026
Awards ceremony: Saturday, November 14, 2026, 1-2:30 PM

SUBMISSION GUIDELINES:

- Only one submission per student will be considered.
- Entries must be the student's original work.
- Submissions should be 2-6 pages (approximately 500 to 1,500 words) and double-spaced.
- Please use MLA General Format standards where applicable.
-

Works must be written in English.

CREATIVE WRITING FORMATS

-

Topic Essay

A topic essay is a short piece of writing on a specific theme or subject.

-

Narrative Essay

A narrative essay recounts a nonfiction story from the narrator's perspective.

-

Persuasive Essay

A persuasive essay aims to persuade the reader to adopt the writer's point of view on a topic.

-

Narrative Poetry

Narrative poetry tells a story and includes elements of storytelling, such as plot and setting, as well as elements of poetry, such as meter and rhyme.

-

Chapbook Poetry

A poetry chapbook is a small collection of poems on a theme or topic.

-

Short Story (any genre – fiction, science fiction, fantasy, horror, romance)

A short story is a brief, fictional prose narrative that is complete in a few scenes.

-

Flash Fiction (any genre – fiction, science fiction, fantasy, horror, romance)

Flash fiction is shorter than a short story but achieves the same effect.

-

Flash Nonfiction

Flash nonfiction is a short piece of writing about a true subject.

-

Monologue

A monologue is a speech delivered by a single person to express their thoughts aloud. It can be serious, humorous, or both.

THIS YEAR'S TOPIC:
Technology and the Future

HOW TO ENTER:
Email submissions with the subject line "Young Writers Contest" to:
swilkinson@sonomalibrary.org

SELECTION CRITERIA:
Please note that the entry you submit for the contest will be evaluated on originality, creativity, relevance to the topic, and adherence to the contest rules. Your writing must be free of spelling or grammatical errors. Please proofread it before submitting. The judging process will be anonymous, and adult members of the local community who are not affiliated with the participating schools or any participants will evaluate submissions.

PRIZES:
First-, second-, and third-place winners will be selected for each grade level (5-9), along with an honorable mention for each grade. First-place winners will receive $100, second-place winners $75, third-place winners $50, and honorable mentions $25.

Writers are encouraged to attend the awards ceremony to celebrate with friends, family, library staff, and volunteers. Teachers and school administrators are likewise encouraged to attend.

PUBLICITY RELEASE:

The winning submissions may be eligible for publication in local news outlets, with permission.

QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS?
Email the Guerneville Regional Teen Services Librarian, Stuart Wilkinson, at swilkinson@sonomalibrary.org

Email: swilkinson@sonomalibrary.org
Phone Number: (707) 869-9004 ext. 0351

events.description:
As we age we lose friends. Some die, some move away, some just... are gone. This is a group for older guys to make friends with other older guys. What do we usually talk about with other guys: sports, politics, the weather? Not in this group. In this group we talk about what's important to us, things like what's going on with our families, what we're glad we did in the past and what we wish we'd done. We talk about what makes us human, and in doing so we discover the many ways we're alike and the ways we're different. In the process we make friends, good friends, friends that we're pleased to have in our lives.

Join us for Volunteer Day in the garden! 

Walk-ins are always welcome – just show up! AND we kindly encourage you to RSVP by clicking the button below (for groups of 6 or more reach out to oaec@oaec.org to schedule so that we can best accommodate your group). Garden volunteers must be 16 years old to participate. 

We serve a homemade garden-based vegetarian lunch for those who come to volunteer for at least 3 hours. We will take a break at 12:30 to eat. Come for part or all of the day – we are happy to have your helping hands for as long as you can participate.

What to bring: In addition to a water bottle, we suggest bringing everything you’ll need to be comfortable outside in all weather – rain gear, an extra layer, hat, sunscreen, sturdy shoes, etc. Bring your own work gloves, if you have them.

events.description:
Library Advisory Board

Members of the public are welcome to attend Library Advisory Board (LAB) meetings. Regional LABs serve to advise the Library Commission on issues affecting each branch.

To learn more about LABs including upcoming meetings visit: sonomalibrary.org/governance/lab

Public comment may be submitted in writing prior to the meeting or orally during the meeting.

- Electronic Writing – Written comments may be submitted via email to to the Branch Manager.
- U.S. Mail – Written comments may be submitted via U.S. mail to the branch's mailing address. It is advised you consider normal delays in mail delivery when sending your written comment via U.S. mail.
- Orally, Live – Oral comments may be given during the meeting.

events.title: Olio Nuovo Harvest and Milling Experience at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
events.address: Gold Ridge Organic Farm, 3387 Canfield Rd, Sebastopol, California, 95472
events.description:
Join us for an unforgettable behind-the-scenes journey into the heart of our olive harvest season. This experience offers a rare opportunity to see how our award-winning olive oil is crafted, from the branches of our olive trees to the first drops of the season’s oil.
Your journey begins with a guided tour of our 88-acre organic farm. You’ll step into the orchards to watch our expert team harvest fresh olives straight from the trees at their peak of flavor.
Next, you’ll visit our state-of-the-art olive oil mill, where you’ll learn about the milling process and see the olives pressed into vibrant, fresh Olio Nuovo, the celebrated “new oil” prized by culinary enthusiasts for its brilliant green hue and robust, peppery finish.
The highlight comes right at the source: tasting fresh Olio Nuovo straight from the mill just moments after the olives are crushed.
Book now to secure your spot for this rare, behind-the-scenes look at our harvest traditions.
Important Notes:
*Please wear comfortable shoes suitable for walking on a working farm
*This outdoor experience may be canceled due to wet weather. Full refund available.

events.title: Harmonic Method for Wellbeing
events.address: Sebastopol Area Senior Center, 167 N High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472, USA
events.description:
Join us as we create a space of connection through toning and rhythm. By vocalizing together—first in unison and then in harmony—we will foster a sense of individual awareness within a supportive, safe group environment. As the session progresses, we will co-create intricate melodic and rhythmic patterns, drawing inspiration from Circle Singing.
Human connection is essential to our well-being. But how can we enhance our ability to give and receive meaningful interactions? Despite our philosophical, social, or personal differences, we all share the experience of being vibrational beings immersed in fields of sound. Our voice is the most intimate, authentic expression of who we are—a window into our emotional and physical health.
In this playful, exploratory session, we will:
Tune into our inner world through silence and listening,
Explore the connection between breath and voice,
Discover vocal resonance, placement, and projection,
Experience the vibrational power of overtones,
Harmonize with others by blending tones and intervals,
Reflect on what harmony feels like and how it can deepen our access to intuition.
After our exploration, we will come together in joyful co-creation with our voices. This group is led by the wonderful Jim Paschal. Learn more about Jim's "Harmonic Method for Well-Being" on his website: Harmonic Method for Well-Being.
Register online at sebastopolseniorcenter.org using your membership key tag code.  OR CALL 707-829-2440

events.title: UC Master Gardeners: All About Growing Beautiful Orchids
events.venue: Sonoma County Library: Northwest Santa Rosa Library
events.address: 150 Coddingtown Center, Santa Rosa, CA, 95401, US
events.org: Sonoma County Library: Northwest Santa Rosa Library
events.sourceLabel: Sonoma County Library: Northwest Santa Rosa Library calendar
events.description:
Orchids are the largest family of flowering plants in the world, with over 25,000 species found in nature, and probably in the order of 150,000 different hybrids. Many think orchids are difficult to grow, but with some basic information, anyone can be successful with growing orchids.

This presentation will cover:

- Understanding the basic needs and care for growing most orchids at home.
- An introduction to the more common orchid groups that are possible to grow.
- Learning which types can grow outside on the Sonoma Coast.

Registration Encouraged: Visit http://sonomamg.ucanr.edu/ Upcoming Events to complete your registration. After registering, you will receive a confirmation email containing information about attending the library talk.

---------------------------------------------------------------

Learn about home gardening, pest management, water conservation practices, and more from your Sonoma County UC Master Gardeners! Different presentation topic per location.

events.title: Old Guys Friendship Group
events.address: Sebastopol Area Senior Center, 167 N High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472, USA
events.description:
As we age we lose friends. Some die, some move away, some just... are gone. This is a group for older guys to make friends with other older guys. What do we usually talk about with other guys: sports, politics, the weather? Not in this group. In this group we talk about what's important to us, things like what's going on with our families, what we're glad we did in the past and what we wish we'd done. We talk about what makes us human, and in doing so we discover the many ways we're alike and the ways we're different. In the process we make friends, good friends, friends that we're pleased to have in our lives.

Register online at sebastopolseniorcenter.org using your membership key tag code.  OR CALL 707-829-2440

events.title: Garden Volunteer Day
events.description:
Join us for Volunteer Day in the garden! 

Walk-ins are always welcome – just show up! AND we kindly encourage you to RSVP by clicking the button below (for groups of 6 or more reach out to oaec@oaec.org to schedule so that we can best accommodate your group). Garden volunteers must be 16 years old to participate. 

We serve a homemade garden-based vegetarian lunch for those who come to volunteer for at least 3 hours. We will take a break at 12:30 to eat. Come for part or all of the day – we are happy to have your helping hands for as long as you can participate.

What to bring: In addition to a water bottle, we suggest bringing everything you’ll need to be comfortable outside in all weather – rain gear, an extra layer, hat, sunscreen, sturdy shoes, etc. Bring your own work gloves, if you have them. 

Please park in the upper lot near the nursery. Read our Contact & Directions page for more arrival information.

PLEASE CHECK THE RSVP FORM FOR HOLIDAYS AND OTHER CLOSURES

events.title: Olio Nuovo Harvest and Milling Experience at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
events.address: Gold Ridge Organic Farm, 3387 Canfield Rd, Sebastopol, California, 95472
events.description:
Join us for an unforgettable behind-the-scenes journey into the heart of our olive harvest season. This experience offers a rare opportunity to see how our award-winning olive oil is crafted, from the branches of our olive trees to the first drops of the season’s oil.
Your journey begins with a guided tour of our 88-acre organic farm. You’ll step into the orchards to watch our expert team harvest fresh olives straight from the trees at their peak of flavor.
Next, you’ll visit our state-of-the-art olive oil mill, where you’ll learn about the milling process and see the olives pressed into vibrant, fresh Olio Nuovo, the celebrated “new oil” prized by culinary enthusiasts for its brilliant green hue and robust, peppery finish.
The highlight comes right at the source: tasting fresh Olio Nuovo straight from the mill just moments after the olives are crushed.
Book now to secure your spot for this rare, behind-the-scenes look at our harvest traditions.
Important Notes:
*Please wear comfortable shoes suitable for walking on a working farm
*This outdoor experience may be canceled due to wet weather. Full refund available.

We will also have tea, so bring your favorite covered drink container.
Sit and Stitch is for people to come and work on any fiber arts activity that they have while visiting with others.
Most people will bring their own projects, but we always have hooks, needles, and yarn and sometimes we will offer a project with instructions that people may choose to make. Let us know what you would like to learn this year. We now have a working sewing machine for people to use. For beginners, I will bring is some fabric to make pillowcases. If you have a project that you would like to work on, bring in your fabric and thread and you can use the machine.

We share ideas, skills, and encouragement with each other.
This summer we will be adding, weaving, and decorative mending to our regular projects of knitting and crocheting.
Children can come if they are accompanied one to one with an adult.

events.title: Old Guys Friendship Group
events.address: Sebastopol Area Senior Center, 167 N High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472, USA
events.description:
As we age we lose friends. Some die, some move away, some just... are gone. This is a group for older guys to make friends with other older guys. What do we usually talk about with other guys: sports, politics, the weather? Not in this group. In this group we talk about what's important to us, things like what's going on with our families, what we're glad we did in the past and what we wish we'd done. We talk about what makes us human, and in doing so we discover the many ways we're alike and the ways we're different. In the process we make friends, good friends, friends that we're pleased to have in our lives.

Register online at sebastopolseniorcenter.org using your membership key tag code.  OR CALL 707-829-2440

events.title: Garden Volunteer Day
events.description:
Join us for Volunteer Day in the garden! 

Walk-ins are always welcome – just show up! AND we kindly encourage you to RSVP by clicking the button below (for groups of 6 or more reach out to oaec@oaec.org to schedule so that we can best accommodate your group). Garden volunteers must be 16 years old to participate. 

We serve a homemade garden-based vegetarian lunch for those who come to volunteer for at least 3 hours. We will take a break at 12:30 to eat. Come for part or all of the day – we are happy to have your helping hands for as long as you can participate.

What to bring: In addition to a water bottle, we suggest bringing everything you’ll need to be comfortable outside in all weather – rain gear, an extra layer, hat, sunscreen, sturdy shoes, etc. Bring your own work gloves, if you have them. 

Please park in the upper lot near the nursery. Read our Contact & Directions page for more arrival information.

PLEASE CHECK THE RSVP FORM FOR HOLIDAYS AND OTHER CLOSURES

Every class includes a warm up, aerobics, weight training, flexibility and 10 balance components. In Chair-Stand SAIL about 50% of the class is held seated and 50% in standing.

It’s fun. It’s safe. It works.

events.title: Latkes, Light & Luncheon: A Cooking Class with Stephanie Klassen Rosenbaum at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
events.address: Gold Ridge Organic Farm, 3387 Canfield Rd, Sebastopol, California, 95472
events.description:
Join us for a seasonal cooking experience celebrating the Festival of Lights that brings together the best of holiday tradition and winter warmth.
In this immersive lunch-and-learn, Stephanie Klassen Rosenbaum will teach you step-by-step how to achieve the perfect crispy, golden potato latke paired with homemade applesauce. She will also share her secrets for crafting a deeply flavorful beet borscht and demonstrate how to elevate simple autumn side dishes—like roasted squash—with our very own award-winning balsamic vinegar.
After learning the techniques, you’ll gather at a cozy communal table to feast on all the dishes prepared. We’ll finish the afternoon on a sweet note with a slice of warm, flaky pie crafted by Red Bird Bakery, featuring Gold Ridge Organic Farms heirloom apples.
What to Expect:
• A scenic ride in our apple-themed trolley from the Farm Shop to the Apple Cottage
• A step-by-step cooking demonstration inside our Apple Cottage kitchen (no cooking required on your part!)
• Expert tips and kitchen secrets from Stephanie Klassen Rosenbaum on crafting traditional dishes using fresh, local produce
• A multi-course sit-down lunch featuring the day’s harvest menu, enjoyed at a communal table in our organic orchard
• Seasonal refreshments, including your choice of a vibrant citrus shrub or our freshly pressed apple cider
• 10% off all Farm Shop purchases on the day of your class
Stephanie Klassen Rosenbaum is the author of seven cookbooks, including A Little Taste of San Francisco and Honey from Flower to Table. She has taught seasonal cooking at farmers markets and other venues from Brooklyn to Berkeley, including the Ferry Plaza Farmers’ Market in San Francisco and the Gravenstein Apple Fair in Sebastopol. She has cooked at numerous artists’ and writers’ retreats including the Headlands Center for the Arts in Sausalito, and studied organic farming at the Center for Agrocology at UC Santa Cruz.

events.title: Harmonic Method for Wellbeing
events.address: Sebastopol Area Senior Center, 167 N High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472, USA
events.description:
Join us as we create a space of connection through toning and rhythm. By vocalizing together—first in unison and then in harmony—we will foster a sense of individual awareness within a supportive, safe group environment. As the session progresses, we will co-create intricate melodic and rhythmic patterns, drawing inspiration from Circle Singing.
Human connection is essential to our well-being. But how can we enhance our ability to give and receive meaningful interactions? Despite our philosophical, social, or personal differences, we all share the experience of being vibrational beings immersed in fields of sound. Our voice is the most intimate, authentic expression of who we are—a window into our emotional and physical health.
In this playful, exploratory session, we will:
Tune into our inner world through silence and listening,
Explore the connection between breath and voice,
Discover vocal resonance, placement, and projection,
Experience the vibrational power of overtones,
Harmonize with others by blending tones and intervals,
Reflect on what harmony feels like and how it can deepen our access to intuition.
After our exploration, we will come together in joyful co-creation with our voices. This group is led by the wonderful Jim Paschal. Learn more about Jim's "Harmonic Method for Well-Being" on his website: Harmonic Method for Well-Being.

events.title: Holiday Cheeseboard Workshop with Alli Keyser-Marti at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
events.address: Gold Ridge Organic Farm, 3387 Canfield Rd, Sebastopol, California, 95472
events.description:
Elevate your holiday entertaining and learn the ultimate skills to wow your guests this festive season!
Join Gold Ridge Organic Farms’ resident cheese expert, Alli Keyser-Marti, for an intimate, hands-on cheeseboard workshop designed to help you create show-stopping displays for your holiday gatherings. Explore how to create your own beautiful board, showcasing a wide array of flavors, textures, and colors. Learn how to incorporate a variety of edible flowers and fresh herbs, local honey, apple cider syrup, balsamic vinegar, EVOO, olives, artisan bread, crackers, and dips to accompany the best local cheeses made by artisan producers from Sonoma County and beyond.
All ingredients and materials included in ticket price. You’ll get to take home your creation to share with friends and family.
Building on a culinary career starting in her teenage years, in 2014 Alli Keyser-Marti fell in love with exploring the world of milk, salt, enzymes, and microbes. Her cheese journey includes managing Cowgirl Creamery’s original Pt Reyes shop, overseeing the Oliver’s Market Stony Point cheese department, as well as being awarded an ACEF Scholarship to attend the American Cheese Society’s Portland conference in 2022, where she successfully completed the Certified Cheese Professional® exam. In 2025, Alli also became an ACS Certified Cheese Sensory Evaluator® and judged cheese for the Good Food Awards. She has followed this passion from her backyard in California to small farms all over France, rural Ohio, roadside stands in Sardinia, and ferries in Croatia. Most recently you’ll find her skillfully pairing cheese with olive oil and apple tastings at Gold Ridge Organic Farms, as well as overseeing our custom olive milling operations and maintaining our organic certifications.

events.title: Gay & Bi Guys Heart Circle Group
events.description:
Title: Gay & Bi Guys Heart Circle Group
Time: 1:30pm - 3:30pm
Facilitator: Scotty King
Cost: Members - FREE   Non-members $10

Come meet your GBT GayBiTrans male Friends and Neighbors. WHAT IS A HEART CIRCLE? Our Heart Circle is a group of men who share, one at a time, how they are feeling. Each person speaks from the heart. No one interrupts and all listen respectfully. It is not a discussion group.  It is not for us to offer advice, to comment or to “fix” anyone. Just be aware that what you say is from your heart, genuine and expresses your real feelings.  Complete and total confidentiality within the group is assumed as a given ground rule.   It is absolutely fine to say nothing if you don’t feel moved to do so. Simply ‘being there’ to witness and hold space for others is equally important.

events.description:
As we age we lose friends. Some die, some move away, some just... are gone. This is a group for older guys to make friends with other older guys. What do we usually talk about with other guys: sports, politics, the weather? Not in this group. In this group we talk about what's important to us, things like what's going on with our families, what we're glad we did in the past and what we wish we'd done. We talk about what makes us human, and in doing so we discover the many ways we're alike and the ways we're different. In the process we make friends, good friends, friends that we're pleased to have in our lives.

events.address: 14107 Armstrong Woods Road, Guerneville, CA, 95446, US
events.org: Sonoma County Library: Guerneville Regional Library
events.sourceLabel: Sonoma County Library: Guerneville Regional Library calendar
events.description:
Sit & Stitch on every Monday 3:30 and 5:30 PM. You can drop in for any amount of time. We have the supplies to help people get started on needle felting, knitting, macrame, and crocheting. We can start needle felting Ornaments and other fun objects for the Holidays.
We will also have tea, so bring your favorite covered drink container.
Sit and Stitch is for people to come and work on any fiber arts activity that they have while visiting with others.
Most people will bring their own projects, but we always have hooks, needles, and yarn and sometimes we will offer a project with instructions that people may choose to make. Let us know what you would like to learn this year. We now have a working sewing machine for people to use. For beginners, I will bring is some fabric to make pillowcases. If you have a project that you would like to work on, bring in your fabric and thread and you can use the machine.

We share ideas, skills, and encouragement with each other.
This summer we will be adding, weaving, and decorative mending to our regular projects of knitting and crocheting.
Children can come if they are accompanied one to one with an adult.

events.title: Young, Gifted, and Black - Art Submissions Due
events.description: Young, Gifted, and Black: Art by Black Students at SRJC is an upcoming exhibition at the SRJC Multicultural Museum celebrating the creativity and artistic voices of Black students across campus. Created in recognition of Black History Month, the exhibition provides a dedicated space for Black student artists to have their work seen, valued, and celebrated by the SRJC community. Black students are invited to submit original artwork in any medium or theme, including visual art, poetry, and other forms of creative writing. Artwork does not need to focus on Black identity or the Black experience—the exhibition celebrates the breadth of Black creativity and the individuality of each participating artist. The exhibition will be on display in the ground floor library display cases from the beginning of the Spring 2027 semester through Spring Break. Students interested in participating must drop off their work at the SRJC Multicultural Museum by December 18, 2026.Learn more about the museum on the SRJC Multicultural Museum website. events.title: Harmonic Method for Wellbeing
events.address: Sebastopol Area Senior Center, 167 N High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472, USA
events.description:
Join us as we create a space of connection through toning and rhythm. By vocalizing together—first in unison and then in harmony—we will foster a sense of individual awareness within a supportive, safe group environment. As the session progresses, we will co-create intricate melodic and rhythmic patterns, drawing inspiration from Circle Singing.
Human connection is essential to our well-being. But how can we enhance our ability to give and receive meaningful interactions? Despite our philosophical, social, or personal differences, we all share the experience of being vibrational beings immersed in fields of sound. Our voice is the most intimate, authentic expression of who we are—a window into our emotional and physical health.
In this playful, exploratory session, we will:
Tune into our inner world through silence and listening,
Explore the connection between breath and voice,
Discover vocal resonance, placement, and projection,
Experience the vibrational power of overtones,
Harmonize with others by blending tones and intervals,
Reflect on what harmony feels like and how it can deepen our access to intuition.
After our exploration, we will come together in joyful co-creation with our voices. This group is led by the wonderful Jim Paschal. Learn more about Jim's "Harmonic Method for Well-Being" on his website: Harmonic Method for Well-Being.
